name: Zheng Yannan
current_role: Founder, Executive Chairman & CEO, Delonix Group (hospitality); founder of 7 Days Inn and Plateno Hotels Group
profile: Most likely Zheng Nanyan (郑南雁, 'Alex Zheng'; Hurun lists the name as 郑雁南), co-founder of Guangzhou budget chain 7 Days Inn (2004/05), which listed on the NYSE in 2009 and was taken private. He then founded Plateno Hotels Group (2013), later sold to Jin Jiang, and since 2022 leads Delonix Group, owner of New Century Hotels and Betterwood Lifestyle Lab.
interesting_fact: 7 Days Inn grew from 5 hotels in 2 cities in 2005 to 283 hotels in 41 cities at its 2009 NYSE IPO, and to about 2,000 hotels in 320 cities by end-2014.
deep_cut_fact: A computer-science graduate of Sun Yat-sen University, he co-founded Armitage Technologies and helped build the Pegasus hotel management system (one of China's top three hotel PMS), then was a VP of Sales & Marketing at Ctrip before founding 7 Days.

name: Tulsibhai Dholakia
current_role: Co-founder, Hari Krishna Exports / Hari Krishna (HK) Group, Surat diamond & jewellery manufacturer
profile: Tulsibhai (Tulsi Dhanji) Dholakia is one of four brothers (with Savji, Ghanshyam and Himmat) who founded Hari Krishna Exports in 1992, now one of India's largest diamond manufacturers/exporters with operations in Surat, Mumbai, Dubai, New York, Hong Kong and Antwerp. He keeps a low public profile; his brother Savji is the family's public face.
interesting_fact: Hari Krishna became internationally known for rewarding employees with cars and flats as Diwali bonuses, including some 600 cars in 2018.
deep_cut_fact: The four brothers started the Hari Krishna Charitable Trust in 1996, which was expanded in 2024 into the Dholakia Foundation, the HK Group's philanthropic arm; in Nov 2025 Tulsibhai attended the group's mass wedding festival at the HK Hub in Surat.
notes: Very low personal profile; almost all coverage is of brother Savji Dholakia. A third-party aggregator (Tofler) shows his HK Exports directorship ending Sept 2024, so his executive role may now be reduced. hk.co blocked automated fetches; trust/foundation detail from company blog via search snippet - verify before using. Best route: HK Group corporate channels.

name: Rajas R Doshi
current_role: Chairman & Managing Director, The Indian Hume Pipe Company Ltd (since 14 April 1994)
profile: Rajas Ratanchand Doshi, a civil engineer from the Walchand-Hirachand business family, has run The Indian Hume Pipe Company (est. 1926), a Mumbai-listed maker of concrete/steel water pipes and builder of water-supply and irrigation projects. He has spent 49+ years at the company and also sits on the boards of family foundations and the IMC Chamber of Commerce.
interesting_fact: Indian Hume Pipe was established in 1926 to manufacture and popularise Hume pipes in India, and today executes large urban and rural water-supply pipeline projects; Doshi has been its chairman for over three decades.
deep_cut_fact: He started at the bottom: a B.E. in civil engineering, he joined Indian Hume Pipe in 1981 as a Senior Executive at its Wadala (Mumbai) factory, then rose via Chief Engineer and General Manager to Joint MD in 1988 and CMD in 1994.
notes: Company emails are corporate (general info / investor relations), not personal. Low media profile; a water-infrastructure angle fits better than energy/data centres.

current_role: General manager (per Baidu Baike), Guangdong Sunion Chemical & Plastic Co. (广东众和化塑), Maoming; current title unverified
profile: Ling Huaming (凌华明) is listed on Baidu Baike as general manager of Guangdong Sunion Chemical & Plastic, a Maoming-based acrylate/chemicals producer founded in 2001 next to the Maoming petrochemical complex. name: Mukesh Aggarwal
current_role: Director / export-side leader, Shivalik Prints Ltd (Faridabad garment & textile group)
profile: Mukesh Aggarwal is a son of Narendra Aggarwal, chairman & MD of Shivalik Prints, a vertically integrated knit/woven textile and garment exporter founded in 1998 in Faridabad. With his brother Nishant he has driven the export business, supplying US/EU retailers such as Walmart, Target, Kohl's, JCPenney and H&M from about nine factories.
interesting_fact: Shivalik started exporting only in 2008, in the middle of the global recession, and within five years was producing ~3.5 million garments a month with 6,000+ sewing machines and 10,000+ workers.
deep_cut_fact: Shivalik built a Rs 3.5 crore water-recycling plant around 2010 that recycles ~85% of its wastewater (over 2 million litres a day), and the group has won Target Sourcing's Vendor Partner Excellence Award.
notes: Wealth shared with father Narendra Aggarwal (Hurun). Little personal coverage; latest detailed profile is from 2013. Several unrelated 'Mukesh Aggarwal's exist in India's corporate registry - don't confuse. Company enquiry email is general, not personal.

name: Deborah E Wiley
current_role: Wiley family shareholder (10%+ owner group, John Wiley & Sons); listed as Secretary & Director, Island Press; former SVP Corporate Communications, Wiley
profile: Deborah E. Wiley is a sixth-generation member of the family that has controlled publisher John Wiley & Sons (founded 1807) and part of the family group holding a 10%+ stake. She worked at Wiley from 1968, ultimately as SVP of Corporate Communications, retiring at the end of 2010, and has chaired the Wiley Foundation.
interesting_fact: She was the first member of the Wiley family's sixth generation to join the business, starting at the company in 1968 and later running its worldwide employee communications and media relations.
deep_cut_fact: As chairman of the Wiley Foundation she oversaw the Wiley Prize in Biomedical Sciences, created by the foundation and first awarded in 2002; she continued chairing the foundation after retiring from the company.

public_contacts.value: brian.campbell@wiley.com (VP Investor Relations, published IR contact)

name: Jonathan A. Brudnick
current_role: Partner, Sachem Head Capital Management; Director, Six Flags Entertainment Corp. (since Oct 2025)
profile: Jonathan Brudnick is a partner at activist hedge fund Sachem Head (since 2017), after earlier roles at private equity and public-market investment firms. He joined the Six Flags board in October 2025 under a cooperation agreement after Sachem Head built a stake of nearly 10% in the theme-park operator formed from the 2024 Cedar Fair-Six Flags merger.
interesting_fact: On joining the board he said Sachem Head invested because 'numerous pathways exist to addressing the Company's current undervaluation', aiming for Six Flags to build on its legacy as 'the premier amusement park company in North America'.
deep_cut_fact: He holds a BBA in finance from Emory University and an MBA from Wharton, and sits on Six Flags' Nominating and Corporate Governance Committee as a Class III director through 2027.

name: Victor Gapare
current_role: Executive Director, Caledonia Mining Corporation Plc (since Jan 2023); ~13% shareholder via Toziyana Resources
profile: Victor Gapare is a Zimbabwean mining entrepreneur who led Bilboes Holdings, a gold miner near Bulawayo, after a 2003 management buyout from Anglo American Zimbabwe. When Caledonia Mining (owner of the Blanket gold mine) acquired Bilboes in January 2023, he received roughly 13% of Caledonia through his family trust's Toziyana Resources and joined its board as an executive director.
interesting_fact: He is a former President of the Chamber of Mines of Zimbabwe and has repeatedly bought Caledonia shares on the open market since joining the board.
deep_cut_fact: Before owning Bilboes he ran it for a multinational: he was Operations Director for Anglo American Corporation Zimbabwe's gold and pyrites business when Bilboes was in its portfolio, and was part of the 2003 management buyout that took it private.
notes: Company general inbox only; Caledonia also publishes IR contacts in its RNS releases. Possible energy angle: Caledonia built a 12.2MW solar plant at Blanket mine to cope with Zimbabwe grid instability (company, not him personally).

name: Daniel Patrick O'Day
profile: Daniel O'Day runs Gilead Sciences, the HIV/antiviral and oncology biopharma, which he joined as chairman and CEO in 2019 after more than three decades at Roche, latest as CEO of Roche Pharmaceuticals (and earlier head of Roche Diagnostics). His wealth comes from Gilead equity compensation; he also serves on the boards of PhRMA and Georgetown University.
interesting_fact: Before Gilead he sat on the boards of Genentech, Flatiron Health and Foundation Medicine while at Roche, and he has served as board chair of the drug-industry trade group PhRMA.
deep_cut_fact: A Georgetown biology graduate, he started at Roche in 1987 in U.S. sales and marketing, earned his Columbia Business School MBA (class of '97) mid-career, and moved to Roche's Basel headquarters in 1998 before rising to run the pharma division.

public_contacts.value: Gilead press releases list media and investor contacts (Gilead corporate communications)

notes: High-profile Fortune 500 CEO; outreach should go through Gilead Corporate Communications. Energy/data-centre angle is weak; better fit is AI in drug development or leadership. Roche start-date/Switzerland move per Columbia/press coverage of his 2018 appointment.

name: Scott C Donnelly
current_role: Executive Chairman, Textron Inc. (since Jan 4, 2026); Director, Medtronic plc
profile: Scott Donnelly (b. 1961) was CEO of Textron, maker of Bell helicopters, Cessna and Beechcraft aircraft and Textron Systems, from Dec 2009 to Jan 2026, and chairman since 2010; Lisa Atherton succeeded him as CEO and he became Executive Chairman. Before Textron he spent ~19 years at GE, rising to CEO of GE Aviation and head of GE Global Research.
interesting_fact: Before running a jet-engine business he ran one of the world's biggest industrial labs: he was senior VP and director of GE Global Research before becoming president & CEO of GE Aviation, then joined Textron as COO in 2008.
deep_cut_fact: He is an electronics engineer by training: his first GE job (1989) was manager of Electronics Design Engineering for GE's Ocean Systems Division in Syracuse, NY, followed by engineering roles in Australia and the US; he has also served on Cornell and Stanford engineering advisory committees.

public_contacts.value: Textron media contact Michael Maynard (phone published, no email)

notes: Good fit for aerospace/eVTOL/engineering topics (Bell, Pipistrel electric aircraft). Route via Textron corporate communications; general enquiries inbox is generic.

name: Ronald G Roth
current_role: Chairman Emeritus and largest shareholder, Clearfield, Inc. (Board Chair 2002 - Feb 2026)
profile: Ron Roth is a Minneapolis-area serial owner-operator and the largest shareholder of Clearfield (NASDAQ: CLFD), a fibre-optic connectivity maker whose products include frames and cabinets for broadband and data-centre networks. He chaired Clearfield's board from 2002 until February 2026, after decades owning and selling waste, recycling and ATM businesses.
interesting_fact: His fortune was built in garbage before fibre: he ran and owned Waste Systems Corp., a waste hauling and disposal firm, from 1970 until selling it to a national solid-waste company in 1995, then chaired Phillips Recycling Systems (1990-2007).
deep_cut_fact: He also chaired and co-owned Access Cash International, a provider of ATMs and payment processing, from 1995 until its sale in 2000; he holds a BA from Michigan State University.
notes: Good data-centre/fibre angle via Clearfield. Very low media profile; route via Clearfield IR (outsourced to Blueshirt Group).

name: Brian H. Franke
current_role: Principal, Indigo Partners LLC; Chair of Volaris (Controladora Vuela); Director, Frontier Group Holdings
profile: Brian Franke has been a principal since 2004 at Indigo Partners, the Phoenix private-equity firm specialising in ultra-low-cost airlines founded by former America West CEO Bill Franke. He has served on Frontier Airlines' board since 2013, on Volaris' board since 2010 (chair since April 2020), and on boards of JetSMART (South America), Cebu Air (Philippines) and airline analytics firm APiJET.
interesting_fact: He sits on the boards of ultra-low-cost carriers on three continents - Frontier (US), Volaris (Mexico, which he chairs), JetSMART (South America) and Cebu Pacific (Philippines) - and earlier on Tiger Airways in Singapore and Australia.
deep_cut_fact: He holds a Master of International Management from Thunderbird School of Global Management (plus a B.S. from the University of Arizona) and served on the University of Arizona Foundation board from 2016 to 2025.
notes: Indigo Partners keeps a minimal public footprint (no published press email found). Route via Frontier or Volaris investor relations. APiJET (real-time airline fuel/cost analytics) could be an energy-efficiency talking point.

name: Kevin T Callahan
current_role: Founding Partner, Fairway Capital Management (Chicago); Trustee & President, Fairway Private Equity & Venture Capital Opportunities Fund
profile: Kevin Callahan (b. 1965), CFA and CPA, founded Chicago private-markets manager Fairway Capital Management in 2017 and runs its registered closed-end fund giving accredited investors access to private equity, private credit and venture funds. He was previously COO of Adams Street Partners (2000-2017), after six years at Brinson Partners and 1987-94 at Arthur Andersen.
interesting_fact: Before founding Fairway he was COO of Adams Street Partners, one of the oldest global private-markets investors, chairing its Operating Committee and heading client service for its fund-of-funds programmes.
deep_cut_fact: Fitting for a firm called Fairway, he is a Trustee of the First Tee of Greater Chicago (the youth golf and life-skills charity), and sits on Chicago Booth's Private Equity Advisory Council; he holds a BS from Ohio State and a Booth MBA.
notes: The ~$60M SEC-derived figure probably reflects fund-level holdings on his filings (he is the fund's president), not necessarily personal wealth. Fund office: One South Wacker Drive, Suite 1050, Chicago (business address from SEC filing). No published email found.

name: Michael Robert Stone
current_role: Founder, FS Investors; Senior Advisor, TPG; independent Director (Audit Committee chair), BETA Technologies
profile: Mike Stone is a private-equity investor: 20 years at J.H. Whitney & Co (1989-2009, retiring as Senior Partner and President), then TPG from 2009, where he was co-managing partner of TPG Growth and CIO of The Rise Fund and TPG Rise Climate. He founded FS Investors, has sat on electric-aircraft maker BETA Technologies' board since 2022 and chairs Anew Climate and Hybar Steel.
interesting_fact: He was Chief Investment Officer of TPG's Rise Climate funds, one of the largest climate private-equity platforms, and now chairs Anew Climate (carbon/RNG solutions) and Hybar Steel (rebar mills) while backing BETA's electric aircraft.
deep_cut_fact: Beyond climate and aviation, he chairs Wilderness Holdings, the African safari-camp owner/operator, and the fast-casual chain Mendocino Farms; he is also a Duke University Trustee (Duke BA in Economics, HBS MBA) and a Hoover Institution overseer.
notes: Excellent energy/climate fit (TPG Rise Climate, Anew Climate, Hybar Steel EAF mills, BETA eVTOL). FS Investors has no public contact page found; BETA/TPG are corporate routes only. Common name - make sure to reference TPG/BETA.

name: Douglas C. Yearley Jr.
current_role: Executive Chairman, Toll Brothers, Inc. (since March 30, 2026; CEO 2010-2026)
profile: Doug Yearley led luxury homebuilder Toll Brothers as CEO from June 2010 - taking over from co-founder Bob Toll after the housing crash - until March 2026, and has chaired the board since 2018; Karl Mistry succeeded him as CEO and he became Executive Chairman. A former commercial litigator, he joined Toll in 1990 and spent 36 years there.
interesting_fact: As Regional President (2005-2009) he oversaw the creation of the Toll Brothers City Living brand, the company's push into urban high-rise condos, and ran its marketing department.
deep_cut_fact: He started as a lawyer: after a Cornell B.S. (1982) and Rutgers J.D. (1986) he was a commercial litigator at New Jersey firm Archer & Greiner, then joined Toll in 1990 doing land acquisitions and project management - he has called joining the company 'the craziest thing I ever did'.
notes: Frequent conference speaker (Wharton Zell Lurie, ULI, Walker & Dunlop webcasts) - podcast-friendly. Route via Toll Brothers corporate communications/IR; no published email found in this pass.
